summary: The Parm Gate: gated_set() validates parm NAMES against the build-keyed catalog before any mutation; a hallucinated name raises a catchable ParmGateError with catalog nearest-match suggestions. reaction_diffusion + pixel_sort kernelcode writes route through it and the parm('kernelcode') or parm('code') phantom hedge is deleted. Runtime lookup API (catalog.parms / catalog.signature) is cheap-exact, embedding-free, degrade-safe. Gate opens no undo path of its own; a gated write lands in the caller's single undo group; rejects only known-bad and degrades to a permissive, observable safe-set otherwise.

acceptance.evidence: tests/test_parm_gate.py::TestRejectionRedGreen::test_red_phantom_name_rejected_with_suggestion ('code' -> ParmGateError, suggestion 'kernelcode'), ::test_green_valid_name_sets ('kernelcode' -> set), ::TestSuggestionQuality (substring + typo ranking, honest-empty on wild miss). Gated against the committed faithful fixture. 25/25 gate tests pass.

findings.claim: Both COP handlers originally discarded gated_set's return, so in DEGRADED mode a dropped kernelcode write (node lacks the parm) was a silent no-op at the handler boundary - violating crucible criterion 3. Surfaced by the adversarial 'silent' lens (CONFIRMED).
findings.fix: handlers_cops.py now captures the gate result and surfaces kernel_written (bool) + kernel_skipped (list) in both handler return dicts. Pinned by tests/test_cops_parmgate_routing.py::test_dropped_kernel_write_is_observable_not_silent.

findings.claim: _handle_cops_set_opencl (:587-598) keeps its multi-name fallback search (kernelcode -> opencl_code/code/snippet) with a terminal 'no kernel parm' error. That is a legitimate arbitrary-node affordance (reached only when kernelcode is absent) covered by test_set_opencl_no_parm; routing it through the strict gate would break that error contract. Left unchanged; out of the named scope (the two scaffolding handlers).

~14 other `parm(X) or parm(Y)` hedges in handlers_cops.py (operation/compop, blursize/size, type/noise_type, size/radius, bright/gain, ...) are REAL cross-version parm-name alternates, not phantom hedges. Gating them needs catalog authority and a multi-candidate gate to avoid false-rejects. Left unrouted this leg; proposed as a follow-up spawn.

reaction_diffusion/pixel_sort's vopcop2gen FALLBACK node (used only if createNode('opencl') returns None) is also routed through the gate. If a FUTURE full catalog knows vopcop2gen WITHOUT a kernelcode parm, gated_set would RAISE where the old hedge silently skipped - turning a degraded scaffold into a hard failure. Cannot bite today (degraded catalog => permissive; fixture lacks vopcop2gen). Re-verify after W5-CATALOG merges. Surfaced by the 'regression' lens as a REFUTED watch item.

Live GUI proof that an artist's single Ctrl+Z REVERSES a gated reaction_diffusion op is UNKNOWN - headless tests prove the undo GROUP is entered around the write, not that the group reverses live. Matches the W5-UNDO/W5-UNDOB posture (grouping only, no rollback). Deferred as a probe-class spawn.
